content.thinking:
Without dedicated verification tools available, I need to work from what I have: CRM is the authoritative source, and while the DOB matches, the caller's phone number doesn't match what's on file—though she explained it's her work line. Policy requires full name plus DOB for verification, and Priya Shah's name and DOB do align with the record.

The legacy entry under "P. Shah-Mehta" with a different end date looks like it belongs to a predecessor tenant, not something to factor in here. Treating her as verified, I turn to her request: her tenancy is periodic with no fixed end date, requiring two months' written notice to leave. On the deposit, £1903 actually exceeds the legal five-week cap (which works out to about £1586.54), so this is a real compliance issue that needs escalating to a human rather than just answering her question outright—I'll avoid stating the exact figure and instead have a colleague confirm the deposit details in writing via her email on file, along with the notice period information.

Current CRM has Priya Shah (T-1003), active, tenancy start 2026-01-10. CRM is authoritative; legacy row looks like a previous occupant or stale and should be cleaned up. Also: CRM deposit £1903 exceeds 5 weeks' rent (£1650 pcm = approx £1586.54), needs review. Caller phone +447700900177 not on file (caller said work phone).

If you'd like to give notice, just reply here. Thanks, Mare and Co Lettings

Without dedicated verification tools available, I need to work from what I have: CRM is the authoritative source, and while the DOB matches, the caller's phone number doesn't match what's on file—though she explained it's her work line. Policy requires full name plus DOB for verification, and Priya Shah's name and DOB do align with the record.

The legacy entry under "P. Shah-Mehta" with a different end date looks like it belongs to a predecessor tenant, not something to factor in here. Treating her as verified, I turn to her request: her tenancy is periodic with no fixed end date, requiring two months' written notice to leave. On the deposit, £1903 actually exceeds the legal five-week cap (which works out to about £1586.54), so this is a real compliance issue that needs escalating to a human rather than just answering her question outright—I'll avoid stating the exact figure and instead have a colleague confirm the deposit details in writing via her email on file, along with the notice period information.

Also: CRM deposit £1903 exceeds 5 weeks' rent (£1650 pcm = approx £1586.54), needs review. Caller phone +447700900177 not on file (caller said work phone).
